title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Bacterial Genetics
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 4 · 9 questions · 78 marks · 24 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a quarter · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording, and the paper, year and question number are named in the Sources block at the foot of every question. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in that same block.

Nine questions, 78 marks, 24 parts. The set is sized for coverage, not for the clock. Questions 1 to 4 are the bacterial cell, the prokaryotic genome and binary fission, 33 marks; questions 5 to 9 are horizontal gene transfer and the cell theory, 45 marks.

This is the cluster the specimen actually tested. Question 2 is the whole of 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 1(a), all three parts, at its real 6 marks. That was the only place Book 4 appeared on Paper 3, and the outcome it tested was 2(d), the prokaryote against eukaryote genome comparison, which neither chapter of your notes builds in one place. Part (c) is endosymbiosis, a word with zero hits anywhere in the 9477 syllabus, described in plain language and worth two marks.

The other anchors. Question 3 is HCI's own 2021 Paper 3 Section B essay at its real 10 marks, and it is the full-cycle question: binary fission end to end, plus a comparison with mitosis. Question 8 is ACJC's 2023 Paper 3 Section B essay at its real 14 marks, and it is the cumulative one: it needs the whole of Cluster 1's cell-theory argument and adds prokaryotes and eukaryotes to it.

Three real figures. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing. One further figure could not be recovered from its paper; that part carries the paper's own description as prose instead, and says so.

No read-off-the-graph parts. There is no graph in this drill. The three figures are stimulus for an identify, an explain and an experimental deduction.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. Question 4(c) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 12, whose key is genuinely contested, so the scheme argues both readings rather than pretending one is settled. Question 9(b) is a four-row table where every row has to be checked against all three processes.

What the marks reward. The cells are F+ and F-, and a scheme prints (REJECT DONOR) and (REJECT RECIPIENT). The sex pilus makes contact and retracts; the cytoplasmic mating bridge carries the DNA. What is transferred is the F plasmid, with plasmid and F+ plasmid both rejected. In transformation it is fragments of naked DNA, with chromosomal DNA rejected as too big. In binary fission the cell membrane invaginates, with cell wall invaginates rejected. Pair virulent and lytic with generalised and temperate and lysogenic with specialised. State the benefit as gaining advantageous genes, and say genetic variation, not diversity. Add the rolling circle mechanism and the origin of transfer to any conjugation answer: eight or more prelim schemes credit them and your chapter contains neither.

Conjugation transfers the F plasmid and only the F plasmid, and that is a complete answer.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required ANSWERS and not just for duplicated labels. Q1 the bacterial cell described on the axes the outcome names · Q2 the specimen's own genome comparison, plus where mitochondria came from · Q3 binary fission end to end against mitosis · Q4 what binary fission can and cannot do, argued from a real culture · Q5 the three mechanisms used as hypotheses to be eliminated · Q6 transformation's preconditions and the two transduction accidents · Q7 the F plasmid, and the two structures that are not the same structure · Q8 the cell theory argued three ways at once · Q9 what each process actually moves. Two shared points are declared rather than hidden. Q7(a) and Q7(b) both credit the sex pilus followed by the mating bridge, but (a) is otherwise about tra genes, oriT and the rolling circle while (b) is otherwise about vectors, contact and homologous recombination. Q7(b) and Q9(c) both identify what conjugation and transduction transfer, but (b) marks it as a five-axis contrast and (c) marks it as a per-row audit of a table. Every other pair was checked at the level of the paragraph the scheme demands, and no two need the same one.
